open_questions: duration ratio 1.686 vs central 1 is long for TIC radius 0.426 Rsun with star_density_penalty 113.6; Gaia radius unknown (needs parallax+spectroscopy) to confirm transit duration and planet radius.

phase_curve amplitude 583.4 ppm ratio_to_depth 0.9351 chi2 147.9/dof 7 indicates stellar variability; rotation period 0.624 d matches signal period at 0.9979 in sectors 3 and 4 and explains most out-of-transit swing without needing a hot binary.

RUWE 14.42 and non_single_star flag suggest astrometric excess/noise, consistent with a spotted/active M dwarf rather than a resolved binary, but high-resolution imaging/spectroscopy could rule out an unresolved companion.
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a shallow 600 ppm, flat-bottomed dip every 0.623 days on the target itself, with no odd-even difference or secondary eclipse and no nearby star that could mimic it. The signal repeats stably over 98 transits and matches a roughly Earth-sized planet, while the long duration and strong 0.62-day stellar wobble likely reflect a small, very active M dwarf rather than a binary.

reasons.why: difference imaging on 2 sectors puts the dip on the target; all neighbours that could fake the 623.9 ppm dip are >53 arcsec and >10 sigma from the centroid, and could_cause_within_1px is 0.
reasons.value: on_target offset 4.233 err 5.099 offset_sigma 0.8303, neighbours plausible_within_1px 0

reasons.why: fit is flat-bottomed, not V-shaped, and ingress fraction 0.1 favours a small transit over a grazing binary.
no odd/even difference at twice the period; binary at 1.25 d ruled out given secondary snr_at_half -5.229 and only 14.36 snr over 98 transits.
implies a 1.17 Earth-radius planet, well below stellar-eclipse sizes, even after accounting for RUWE 14.42 dilution.
apparent 45% sector depth change is calibration between QLP and SPOC, not astrophysical change; transit_depths p_consistent 0.8765 over 98 transits shows no flickering outliers and share top-3 0.129.
